Name: Alexander of Ephesus
Summary: Alexander was a man put forward by the Jews during the Ephesian riot, who tried to address the theatre crowd in defence of his people, but was shouted down when the crowd recognised him as a Jew. He is distinct from Alexander son of Simon of Cyrene and from Alexander named in the later epistles.
KeyStory: Alexander was thrust forward to speak in the theatre and drowned out by two hours of shouting.
LifeLesson: A crowd in uproar hears no defence. Alexander's silence warns us against reasoning with a riot.
